headline: Ingham's CEO highlights poultry as a resilient consumer category benefiting from cost-of-living pressures and ongoing volume growth of ~3%
reasoning: Alexander described poultry as an 'incredibly resilient category' that benefits when consumer budgets are under pressure from cost-of-living challenges. The category is seeing ongoing volume growth of around 3% per annum, which Ingham's expects to continue. Additionally, there is a noticeable shift from out-of-home to in-home consumption as Middle East crisis-related cost-of-living pressures intensify, which further supports the retail poultry segment.
quote: I think you know what we're seeing is poultry remains you know incredibly resilient category. You know it's the category that you want to be playing in. You know where cost of living is difficult. We're sort of seeing ongoing growth of around about that 3%. And we expect that continue. We're certainly seeing a little bit of switching from out-of-home consumption to in-home consumption, over the last few months, you know, particularly as cost of living, you know, related to the Middle East crisis starts to bite.
episode_title: Ingham's looks to hatch a recovery

headline: Ingham's CEO says bird flu poses industry-wide risk but geographically diversified national network provides relative biosecurity advantage
reasoning: Alexander acknowledged that bird flu casts a long shadow over the Australian and New Zealand poultry industry. He argued that at an industry level, preparedness is strong with government engagement and learnings captured from UK and US outbreaks. At the company level, Ingham's national footprint has been specifically designed to manage biosecurity risk, which he believes makes the company better placed than other players to mitigate potential impacts from an outbreak at any single facility.
quote: Bird flu obviously is a pretty long shadow that hangs over the industry across Australia and to a slightly lesser extent, New Zealand at the moment. What I would say, firstly at industry level I think we're really well prepared. There's been a lot of engagement with government and people overseas to understand learnings, capture learnings from the UK and the US, and I think there's good agreements in place in terms of how we respond in the event of an outbreak. I then say that from Inghams perspective, we've got a national network, a national footprint that's been specifically designed to manage biosecurity risk. So at that level, I'd say we're better prepared there, probably any other player within the industry to ensure that we mitigate the effects and impacts of bird flu in one of our operations.
episode_title: Ingham's looks to hatch a recovery
